title: aggregate query answers wrong data under 200: dateGranularity on a non-date field, a duplicate alias, and an alias equal to a groupBy field
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a live reproduction. The aggregate door answers silently wrong numbers under 200, finding class (a).
Business reason: a report, dashboard or AI caller that builds an aggregate gets a plausible-looking but wrong table: counts overwritten, group keys destroyed, every row in one bucket. Nothing tells it the request was malformed, which is the silent-coercion shape AGENTS.md route rules forbid ("absence must be loud").
Reader: the `packages/objectql` / protocol aggregate lane (the refusal belongs beside `assertAggregationFieldsExist` and the unknown-groupBy refusal); the next PR touching aggregate validation.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "aggregate query duplicate alias overwritten or dateGranularity on non-date field returns 200" → 11 hits, none of them this one. The nearest are #21437 (empty measure prefix → 500) and #20123 (unknown `having` key), both different doors.
reach: public HTTP entry, measured on a fresh stock showcase boot, `main` 6679644a, as admin. Each shape was reproduced twice.
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug
QA-source: #25817 · api-backend.aggregate-contract-matrix · observed beside the clauses

The aggregate door is `POST /api/v1/data/showcase_account/query`. Each of these bodies answers 200 with a wrong result:

| body | answer | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `{"groupBy":[{"field":"name","dateGranularity":"month"}],"aggregations":[{"function":"count","alias":"n"}]}` | `200 [{"name":null,"n":16}]`: every row lands in one null bucket | 400, naming `groupBy.0.dateGranularity` on a non-date field |
| `{"aggregations":[{"function":"count","alias":"n"},{"function":"sum","field":"annual_revenue","alias":"n"}]}` | `200 [{"n":682700000}]`: the count is silently overwritten by the sum | 400, naming the duplicate alias |
| `{"groupBy":["status"],"aggregations":[{"function":"count","alias":"status"}]}` | `200 [{"status":10},{"status":2},{"status":4}]`: the group keys are replaced by counts | 400, naming the alias that collides with a groupBy field |

The same door already refuses an unknown groupBy field, explaining that otherwise every row would fall into one null bucket. These three shapes are that hazard reached by another path.
